blocks.text: Phyllodocidae are sometimes known as paddle-worms owing to their (usually) large and flattened dorsal cirri. The holopelag- ic Alciopidae (see Pl. 5h) are previously treated as a separate taxon in the literature but is here included in Phyllodocidae Alciopini. Similarly, we also consider the small and poorly as known holopelagic group Iospilidae (Figs. 24.2a-c) as a junior of Phyllodocidae and included them herein, a place- synonym supported by molecular data (San Martin et al., 2021; ment comm.). However, due their uncertain position Rouse, pers. to Phyllodocidae here refer them ‘iospilids’. As far as is known, iospilids are also transparent, though segmental pigment spots may be present on the antero-dorsal side of the parapodia.
